author: Sophia Lam
title: Magnitude 4.8 Earthquake Hits Xinjiang Near India-China Border
text:
A magnitude 4.8 earthquake struck a remote mountainous area of China’s Xinjiang region early Friday, with shaking reportedly felt in parts of neighboring Indian-administered Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir, according to Chinese and Indian seismic agencies.

initiallyestimated the magnitude at about 5.1 before revising it to 4.8.
The earthquake was centered in Hotan Prefecture in southern Xinjiang, at 35.64 degrees north latitude and 78.14 degrees east longitude, according to the center.
reporteda magnitude of 5.0 and a depth of 164 kilometers (102 miles), placing the epicenter at 35.587 degrees north latitude and 78.130 degrees east longitude. The agency said it had received reports of shaking in Jammu and Kashmir.
Volcano Discoveryalso listed the quake at magnitude 5.0, but estimated its depth at 77 kilometers (nearly 48 miles).
The service said residents of Thang, an Indian town about 81 miles southwest of the epicenter, may have experienced weak shaking.
reportedthat the earthquake struck near the Ladakh border late Thursday local time and that tremors were felt in parts of Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir.
Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that the area within 5 kilometers (3 miles) of the epicenter has an average elevation of about 5,633 meters (18,481 feet). No township centers are located within 50 kilometers (31 miles), while Hongliu Township is among the settlements within 100 kilometers (62 miles). The epicenter was about 109 kilometers (68 miles) from Hotan County, CCTV reported.
There were no immediate reports of casualties or property damage, according to CCTV. Traffic, electricity and telecommunications services, as well as residents’ daily activities, were reported to be operating normally, according to Chinese state media.
Reutersthey hadn’t received as much information as they wanted from China on glacier risks and water levels before the disaster.
Several Earthquakes Recorded in Xinjiang
The latest earthquake follows several other magnitude 4 or stronger earthquakes recorded in Xinjiang in recent days, according to the China National Earthquake Data Center.
4.1 earthquakestruck Toksun County in Turpan, at a depth of 15 kilometers (9 miles).
4.3 quakestruck Hutubi County in Changji Hui Autonomous Prefecture at 4:19 a.m., at a depth of 20 kilometers (12 miles).
